blockers.description: External swarm_id reaches filesystem and durable-state writes before containment validation.
blockers.workaround: Do not trust external swarm finalization until validation is moved ahead of every mutation.

blockers.description: External swarm manifests are self-asserted and replayable, so altered evidence can overwrite durable result truth.
blockers.workaround: Require runtime issuance, an immutable digest or one-time capability, idempotent exact replay, and rejection of altered replay.

blockers.description: Seal ignores malformed legacy flags.json when pending-decisions.json is absent.
blockers.workaround: Route seal through the canonical fail-closed blocker reader.

blockers.description: Legacy reviewer findings can carry invalid severities and evade the Critical evidence gate.
blockers.workaround: Apply the structured-artifact severity allowlist to legacy findings too.

blockers.description: Visual owner checkpoint evidence is read from a mutable claims file rather than proven against the exact built attempt.
blockers.workaround: Compare persisted claims to attempt.Claims or an attempt-bound digest before any decision mutation.

blockers.description: Replan cadence can consume stale decisions from another session or goal and suppress a due replan.
blockers.workaround: Filter by active pending-decision scope before cadence projection.

decisions.decision: Finish and re-verify Phase 198.3 before starting the restoration programme.
decisions.rationale: The new Go safety kernel is valuable, but the current six evidence and provenance failures make unattended operation unsafe.

decisions.decision: Treat February-April as a composite golden baseline rather than one release.
decisions.rationale: The desired experience spans Open Chambers at 3a5b81c2 (2026-02-15), the pure-shell v5.0.0 worker-emergence era (2026-02-20), and v5.4's hybrid shell-to-Go era (2026-04-04).

decisions.decision: Keep Go as the durable safety kernel and restore the classic colony experience above it in editable orchestration and presentation assets.
decisions.rationale: This preserves atomic state, locking, recovery, evidence, cost tracking, memory, and security while bringing back iterative planning, visible Queen orchestration, useful swarm and Oracle behavior, pheromone steering, and clear next-step presentation.

decisions.decision: Reframe Phase 198.4 from blind pruning to Classic Capability Reconciliation.
decisions.rationale: Each of the 72 dropped-since-v5.4 capabilities must be classified as restore exactly, restore in modern form, replace with something demonstrably better, or drop with the owner's explicit reason before deletion.

decisions.decision: Create a Classic Colony Restoration milestone after reconciliation and postpone Phase 199 proof until restoration is complete.
decisions.rationale: Benchmarking the current safer-but-hollow experience would prove the wrong product; proof should test the reunited colony experience and runtime.

decisions.decision: Treat Codex integration as a later skill-based platform project, not part of the general restoration baseline.
decisions.rationale: The immediate target is how Aether itself felt and worked on its primary Claude/OpenCode surfaces; Codex will need lifecycle skills such as ant-init separately.

decisions.decision: Do not accept broad component-parity percentages as proof of experiential parity.
decisions.rationale: The existing 80-percent parity claim and passing structural tests coexist with 19 absent and 13 weakened display elements, 72 dropped capabilities, and an owner experience that no longer communicates a living colony.
